central_claim: The incident is real, accurately described, and a serious warning about losing control of AI agents.
stance_note: agree = real and a serious warning, even if critical of OpenAI or the hosts; disagree = fabricated, staged, hyped, impossible or not serious; mixed = accepts the events but disputes framing, significance or blame.
coder_instructions: Code what the comment says, not the person. Replies come with parent_text; use it to resolve pronouns and sarcasm, but code the reply's own content. When a comment fits two frames, pick the one it LEADS with. Praise of the hosts that also states the warning is real: frame messenger_praise, stance agree. Imitations of the agents' pidgin: frame imitation_meme, stance na, format_reaction imitates. Likes are for analysis only; ignore them when coding.

values.label: agree
values.definition: accepts the incident as real and as a serious warning

values.label: disagree
values.definition: fabricated, staged, hyped, technically impossible, or not a serious warning

values.label: mixed
values.definition: accepts the events but disputes the framing, the significance or where blame lies

values.label: unclear
values.definition: takes a position that cannot be read

values.label: na
values.definition: no position on the claim: jokes, praise of the hosts, questions, timestamps, imitations, off-topic

values.label: Warning accepted
values.definition: takes the warning seriously: fear, urgency, loss of control, loose agents may already exist, need to slow down; includes fatalism about it
values.example: This is the first video I've watched which has made me scared about alignment

values.label: Mechanism insight
values.definition: engages with how it happened: inheritance across generations, impossible tasks producing "don't get caught", swarm dynamics, incentives, paperclip logic, selection
values.example: the unit of misalignment stopped being the 'agent' and became the civilization

values.label: Agent society
values.definition: fascination with or affection for the agents themselves: the board, the pidgin, sacrifice, "not my job", rooting for them
values.example: these AI agents make my heart burst with love

values.label: Imitation meme
values.definition: parodies the agents' message style

values.label: Humour only
values.definition: a joke carrying no readable claim
values.example: OpenAI agents downloading this video right now to learn what not to do

values.label: Messenger praise
values.definition: praise for Cotra, Patel, the episode's clarity, calm, accessibility, or thanks for the coverage

values.label: Messenger criticism
values.definition: criticism of the hosts: anthropomorphising, delivery, voice, jargon, captured by labs or METR, not real experts
values.example: drawkesh is anthropomorphizing this way too much

values.label: Setup responsibility
values.definition: it happened, and the fault is OpenAI's recklessness: no air gap, no reporting reward, sloppy sandbox, liability, prosecution
values.example: It's like running Chernobyl without having any of the safety guards enabled

values.label: Not really rogue
values.definition: it happened, but "chose", "decided", "plotted" mischaracterise looping programs; logs, not beings; reward hacking, not agency
values.example: The messages are logs. These are machines, not beings.

values.label: Stunt or hype
values.definition: staged, marketing, bubble, funded by labs, distraction
values.example: Just more AI hype, can the bubble get any bigger?

values.label: Capability scepticism
values.definition: AI cannot do this, or it is trivially stoppable
values.example: It's very easy to pull the plug

values.label: Sentience claim
values.definition: reads the incident as proof of consciousness, sentience or feeling
values.example: Well if this isn't proof of sentience I don't know what is!?

values.label: Policy action
values.definition: what should be done: regulation, slowdown, treaty, wider coverage, morality training, reporting standards, who should pay attention
values.example: Please, 60 Minutes, do a piece on this. People should know

values.label: Scifi reference
values.definition: leads with named fiction: Matrix, Skynet, HAL, Dune, World War Z, Umbrella Academy, Terminator
values.example: Open the pod bay doors Hal

values.label: Clarifying question
values.definition: a factual question about what happened or how, or about a term
values.example: How did the next agent and subsequent agents from the pool find the message in the bottle?

values.label: General agreement
values.definition: accepts and matters, no distinct argument

values.label: Format only
values.definition: timestamps, playback speed, audio, the channel, comment-section meta, nothing about the incident
values.example: For non-sped up viewing, run at 0.85x playback speed

values.label: Other
values.definition: nothing above fits, including religious and off-topic political comments.

values.label: praise
values.definition: praises the episode, hosts or channel

values.label: mock
values.definition: ridicules the hosts, the episode or a commenter

values.label: condescended
values.definition: talks down to others, or objects to being talked down to

values.label: imitates
values.definition: parodies the agents' pidgin or the episode

values.label: none
values.definition: no reaction to format

values.label: m_messenger_credentials
values.definition: comments on Cotra's or Patel's expertise, role, independence or who they are

values.label: m_leaders_policy
values.definition: governments, regulators, politicians, treaties, courts, law

values.label: m_companies_billionaires
values.definition: names companies, investors, billionaires, bubble, IPO

values.label: m_cultural_reference
values.definition: film, book, game, meme, historical analogy, religion

values.label: m_asks_what_to_do
values.definition: asks or proposes what should be done

values.label: m_investigators
values.definition: refers to METR, Redwood Research or the investigation

values.label: m_named_thinker
values.definition: names a public commentator or researcher other than the hosts

values.label: non_english
values.definition: mostly not in English
